title: Giving in the Church
definition: Giving in the Church is the generous, cheerful, and faithful sharing of resources for worship, ministry, mercy, and mission.
summary: Giving in the Church is worshipful stewardship that supports ministry, mercy, mission, and the needs of the body.
christFocus: Jesus Christ gave Himself for us, and His grace teaches His people to give freely and joyfully.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Giving in the church is the joyful, willing support of Gospel ministry, mercy, and shared needs. Scripture connects giving with worship, stewardship, generosity, and love for the body.

Christian giving is not manipulation, showmanship, or payment for blessing. It is a grace-shaped response to God, done with integrity and cheerful purpose.

Jesus gave Himself for His people. The church's giving should reflect His generosity without turning generosity into pressure or pride.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because giving can be abused by leaders or avoided by members. Biblical giving protects both: it calls for generosity while demanding honesty, humility, and care with resources entrusted to the church.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Give prayerfully, willingly, and responsibly as God enables you. Leaders should handle gifts transparently, and believers should see giving as worship and shared mission, not religious dues.
